newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila plans 300,000 T-350,000 T sugar imports.
newsitem.headline: Manila plans 300,000 T-350,000 T sugar imports.

text.p: The Philippines' Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) plans to import between 300,000 and 350,000 tonnes of sugar for the 1997/98 year (Sept-Aug) for buffer stocks, SRA chief Wilson Gamboa said on Friday.
"I will recommend the importation of sugar to President Ramos at the earliest in September this year as a security reserve," Gamboa told reporters.
Domestic demand for sugar is expected to reach 2.1 million tonnes for the next crop year.
"I expect a shortage of 300,000 tonnes to 350,000 tonnes," Gamboa said.
The proposed sugar imports will be used as reserve for a two month period, the official added.
Last month, the SRA approved the imports of 27,000 tonnes to compensate for the volume of additional exports to the U.S.
The Department of Agriculture expects Philippine raw sugar output to increase to 1.9 million tonnes for the present crop year.
